subject: Follow-up: deployment mode and noisy-neighbor concerns
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Tom Baxter <tom.baxter@acmeinc.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: deployment mode and noisy-neighbor concerns

Hi Tom / Laura —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps while it's fresh:

What we heard:
- Primary goal: move inference for your chat product into production with predictable latency; target ~<200ms P50 for session generation and consistent tail behavior.
- Traffic profile (ballpark): ~8–12 req/s sustained, spiky peaks up to ~25 req/s; average request ~120 tokens output.
- Main concern: noisy-neighbor effects on shared Hosted API that could increase tail latency during noisy periods.

Clarifying questions to help recommend an approach:
1) Can you confirm peak concurrent requests and whether you have any strict SLAs for customers?
2) Any specific compliance/network constraints that would push you to Private VPC sooner?

High-level options we discussed: Hosted API (fastest to prod), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools - predictable throughput/isolation), Private (VPC/on-prem for strict isolation). Based on what you said about tail risk, Dedicated is often the right balance: isolation + predictable throughput without the full ops of a Private deployment.

Attachments: Redwood-Dedicated-Overview.pdf (quick overview), SLA-summary.pdf (SLO/SLA examples).

Next steps I recommend:
- Short (30m) technical sync with your infra lead + our solutions engineer (Marissa) to walk isolation boundaries and run a quick capacity worksheet.
- If that looks good, we can provision a 2-week Dedicated trial with monitoring to verify tail latency under your workload.

When are you available next week? I can get Marissa and Vivek on the call.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Tom Baxter <tom.baxter@acmeinc.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmeinc.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode and noisy-neighbor concerns

Thanks Priyom — great summary. A couple of quick things from our side:

- We can confirm peaks of ~25 req/s and bursts up to ~40 req/s during marketing-driven traffic. Concurrency at peak tends to be ~12–15.
- Our compliance team prefers not to go on-prem right away; Private VPC is an option but would add procurement overhead.

Specific question on Dedicated vs Hosted: what isolation guarantees do you make for Dedicated capacity? In particular, how do you mitigate noisy neighbors on Hosted (does Redwood do request shaping, fair-queueing, or hard cgroups on shared infra?), and what SLAs would you commit to for latency/tail behavior on Dedicated?

Procurement will probably push us toward keeping things on Hosted if the tail risk is low — any quantitative numbers you can share from similar customers would help.

-Tom
Senior Engineering Manager, Acme Chat

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Baxter <tom.baxter@acmeinc.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode and noisy-neighbor concerns

Hi Tom / Laura —

Happy to jump in with some detail on isolation and mitigations. Short answers first: Dedicated = tenant-dedicated GPU pools with strict isolation and predictable throughput; Hosted has multiple mitigations but cannot provide the same hard isolation guarantees as Dedicated.

Key details:
- Hosted API mitigations:
  • Dynamic fair-queueing and per-tenant soft rate limits to reduce interference.
  • Continuous batching and adaptive scheduling prioritizes latency-sensitive routes.
  • Prefix/KV caching reduces work for repeat traffic patterns.
  • However, because resources are shared, extreme noisy workloads can increase queuing/tails for co-tenants during capacity contention.

- Dedicated capacity (what you get):
  • Dedicated GPU pool assigned to your account — no other tenants placed on those hosts.
  • Per-tenant scheduler and hard resource isolation (cgroup-like enforcement) for CPU/GPU and memory.
  • Predictable throughput scaling: reserved slots for burst capacity and configurable autoscaling policies.
  • KV cache and KV encryption keys scoped to your tenant; no cross-tenant cache leakage.
  • Monitoring/alerts: token-level latency histograms, P50/P95/P99 dashboards, and exportable traces for debugging.

- SLO/SLA:
  • We publish SLO guidance for Hosted vs Dedicated. Dedicated throughput/latency SLOs are tighter because of hard isolation; we can provide a Dedicated SLA addendum in contracts (see attached SLA-summary.pdf).

If helpful, we can run a short “capacity worksheet” during the next call: we need qps, avg tokens per request, expected concurrency, and traffic profile over 24h. With that we can size a Dedicated pool and give a pricing delta estimate versus Hosted.

Proposed times: Thu 12/3 10:00–10:30am PT or Fri 12/4 9:00–9:30am PT. Let me know what works.

Thanks,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmeinc.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode and noisy-neighbor concerns

Thanks Marissa — that helps. A few follow-ups from procurement and product:

- Procurement: can you give a ballpark of the monthly cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated for the sizing you mentioned (approximate is fine, we just want to know if Dedicated is a 10% vs 2x cost uplift).
- Product: if we go Dedicated, how long to spin up a trial environment? We want something we can run real traffic against (not synthetic) for ~2 weeks.
- Private VPC: if Dedicated doesn't meet our compliance bar, how long does a Private VPC deployment typically take?

Procurement is likely to push for Hosted unless the delta on tail risk is significant. If you can give a short pricing range and a timeline for a Dedicated trial, that will help internal alignment.

Best,
Laura
Director of Product, Acme Chat

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmeinc.com>, Tom Baxter <tom.baxter@acmeinc.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode and noisy-neighbor concerns

Great questions — quick answers and concrete next steps:

1) Pricing delta (ballpark): Dedicated typically ranges from ~1.4x–2.0x Hosted for the same sustained QPS depending on reserved capacity and burst needs. We'll provide a tailored range after the worksheet but expect the premium for hard isolation.

2) Dedicated trial timeline: we can provision a 2-week Dedicated trial within 48–72 hours after we get the sizing worksheet and a signed trial T&Cs. The trial environment supports real traffic and telemetry so you can validate tail behavior.

3) Private VPC timeline: Private VPC onboarding usually takes 4–8 weeks depending on network approvals and any custom compliance work; we can provide a checklist to speed that up.

Next steps I can own this week:
- Schedule the 30m capacity call (Marissa + Vivek joining). Please pick Thu 12/3 10:00am PT or Fri 12/4 9:00am PT — Marissa suggested those times; if neither work we can pick another window.
- I’ll send the sizing worksheet and a short trial T&Cs doc. Required inputs: sustained qps, peak qps, avg output tokens, typical concurrency, desired P95/P99 targets, and any compliance flags.
- I’ll also attach the HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/67890 and add procurement contact to the thread if you want.

If that sounds good I’ll schedule for Thu 12/3 10:00am PT and circulate a calendar invite.

Best,
